decisions.reason: L7 cited a completeness definition for sequential compactness. Replaced it with the choice-free compact-to-sequential-compact supplier (clauses 1 and 3), the metric/topological compactness equivalence, and the Cauchy-subsequence lemma. Step 4.1 now extracts its limit from the compact sublevel in the same distance topology; AC_omega completeness hypotheses and Statement are unchanged.

Chronology openness is declared in justified_by, not deps: SCHEMA.md expressly permits well-definedness suppliers to depend on the definition they justify. The future-set predicates use only I^+(F) subset F; chronological openness and push-up discharge the listed derived properties. No reverse prerequisite edge or circular proof premise is introduced.

The title claimed convexity of |x| while the exact Statement and proof concern |x|^2. Corrected only the title. The geodesic equation yields f second derivative at least 2(1-GammaNorm |x|)|x prime|^2; the convex chord estimate gives the asserted radius bound without claiming convexity of its square root.

The proof evaluated at (0,0) and selected origin-centered balls without centering its chosen chart. Explicitly translated x(p) to zero in step 1.2 and restricted L5 to that centered chart. The inverse-function domain can then be restricted to an open product, whose image contains a closed smaller pair; the coordinate derivative bound gives clause (d). Statement unchanged.

The one-sided reciprocal derivative estimate was misattributed to a two-sided Lipschitz corollary. L2 now proves it by FTC for the smooth reciprocal. Step 1.1 uses geodesic uniqueness to ensure nonvanishing speed before division; integration gives w <=4v0/3 and the 7v0 delta/9 displacement bound implies the stated weaker 5/9 bound and contained velocity <=4r. No Statement change.

Clause (b) omitted convex normality from the strict predicate, so later use of normal inverses did not follow from that predicate. Added that exact missing requirement, retaining the unique closure geodesic and equal-endpoint convention. Consulted Minguzzi Definition 2.3, which imposes both conditions; the local existence theorem already proves both.

The base point p is arbitrary in the theorem and in the initial-cone lemma. Step 2.2 applies the already proved containment argument separately to each subarc, rebasing the second at q; C is normal at every q by the repaired strict definition and L1. Reversing that causal radial geodesic contradicts unique contained geodesics. The fixed-p notation does not restrict this universal application; no edit is needed.

The claimed joint-inverse regularity is proved in the supplier Fact L4, not asserted by its clause (c). Corrected that locator and stated its local IFT/contained-geodesic argument. The compact fixed-branch estimates, first-exit identification with arbitrary selected inverses, Lebesgue-point speed limit and Fatou control establish refined sums and upper semicontinuity without requiring a global near-diagonal chart. Statement unchanged.

L5 already assumes membership in the closed future cone before using the positive time component to exclude zero; it does not assert that a positive component alone decides orientation. Step 6.1 first puts the derivative in that cone by scaled future position-vector limits. Separately repaired the digest-confirmed chart-scope defect: a3 now specifies the buffered chart actually used in L6, and step 5.2 uses a matrix operator norm. An unbuffered chart can have unbounded h coefficients; the causal-limit conclusions are preserved.

The phrase auxiliary metric failed to specify the complete rescaled h-prime and described a global metric on possibly disconnected M. Explicitly chose the supplier conformal metric and made distances componentwise; eventually all joining curves lie in the component of x. L4 now cites precisely the compact-ball conclusion used in 1.1. Positive, zero and infinite length alternatives and endpoint/closure conclusions are preserved.

L1 incorrectly excluded purely temporal future timelike displacements from the future-causal criterion. Corrected it to v0 >= spatial norm for nonzero v, which then implies v0>0. Both worked null legs, the timelike total displacement and the parallel null comparison satisfy this criterion; the constructive chronology proof was already sound. No Example or Statement change.

Step 5.1 selected a parameter for every point of an arbitrary compact set without licensed arbitrary choice. Replaced this with covers containing all admissible parameters and finite subcovers, including the empty case. Also corrected the digest-confirmed false converse in Remarks: the proof establishes only the forward implication; a compact totally vicious flat torus disproves the unqualified converse. Clarified use of the complete conformal metric. Statement unchanged.

L1 used U=M, which cannot exclude any intermediate point and does not violate strong causality. Replaced it with U=M minus a distinct image point of the nonconstant loop; every allowed smaller V then has both endpoints in V and the loop leaves U. The closed-cone indicator argument, null boundary, dominated convergence and strict chronological volume comparison now use that valid no-loop proof. Statement unchanged.

L5 did not distinguish the complete conformal auxiliary metric from its unscaled precursor. Fixed h as the supplier h-prime throughout the proof and cited its proved absolutely continuous distance-length inequality in L6. Finite total h-length makes the cofinal image Cauchy in the same complete component, contradicting inextendibility. Also justified distinct intermediate endpoints by absence of closed causal subcurves. Statement unchanged.

L1 incorrectly made the reflexive causal level regions strict. Replaced them by t>=b and t<=b, retaining I+(S_a)={t>a}; this makes p in K immediate. Also supplied the missing neighborhood plateau construction in L5 using a finite cover by nested chart balls and 1-product(1-chi_i), so the weaker Euclidean cutoff supplier is used accurately without arbitrary choice. The cone-gradient, flat-zero and diameter claims retain their Statement.

The cited Euclidean cutoff statement supplies equality on K, not a neighborhood of K. L5 now first thickens K to a compact K1 inside C using a finite ball cover, and applies that exact supplier to K1. Its interior supplies the plateau used to erase the cutoff gradient on the truncated cone. The flat branch and gradient calculations and all claimed bump properties are unchanged.

The normal-neighborhood existence theorem establishes geodesic geometry, while the separate causal-cone theorem proves the advertised causal and length calculus. Added that actual prerequisite and split the references accurately. Also corrected complete gradient flow to complete flow of X=grad T/g(grad T,grad T), the field whose completeness is established. The declared physical scope and absence of empirical conclusions are unchanged.

The supplier Statement only asserts the half-time Cauchy slice. Added the exact flat time-increment and Euclidean completeness suppliers and proved all slices in step 1.1: any interior time-end limit forces a spatial Cauchy limit in the slab, so inextendible curves have time range (0,1). Also consistently named X as the normalized gradient field. Its maximal vertical domain (-1/2,1/2) proves the refutation with the original Statement refuted intact.
